summary: Read the captured OmniPaxos core and async-runtime sources and registered one sourced client-completion question: drain_notifiers resolves Ok(idx) before the ballot-superseded arm and without checking that the decided value at idx is the caller's entry, so an append_notify whose locally accepted entry was replaced at the same index may be acknowledged as decided. Added three knowledge entries (drain ordering, Ok-means-caller-entry test expectation, Superseded replacement witness), one active investigation with an unresolved defect claim, and a gap on the decisive actor interleaving. No experiment ran: omnipaxos_runtime is not a dev-dependency of the omnipaxos assurance test target, so the false-Ok timeline and log-content identity remain unverified.
